Reply source

🧠 one reply · the reasoning and the network averaged
there is no engine to pick. Every reply is a single answer drawn from the average of two things that know something: what the network predicts next, and what the reasoning judged relevant to your turn. The slider is how much of that average is the reasoning's half — at 0 the network answers alone, at 1 the reasoning does.
advanced reply controls
a reply is read out of your connections: the word you asked about, the verb the graph holds for it, and its top associations by reasoned strength — joined with commas and "and". top phrases sets how many phrases, words per term the most associations each may carry — the reply itself speaks at most three (two when the turn asks for a specific kind of word), so a long list is never read out as an answer. Turn reasoning weight down for wording the network produces on its own, and up for wording taken from your connections. The working-out is in the bar above each reply.
the test button shows what the network produces with no reasoning mixed in at all.

Impulse engine

⚡ impulse: online
dopamine (tonic)0.50
pain (aversive)0.05
reward prediction error—
feedback given👍 0 · 👎 0
words carrying a signal0
weight updates from feedback0
Every reply carries 👍 reward / 👎 punish buttons. What moves the engine is the reward prediction error - the verdict minus what the reply's own confidence led it to expect - so a 👍 it expected teaches almost nothing and a surprise teaches most. A 👎 also marks the words of that reply aversive for a few turns, so the engine stays off them. Then it trains: a verdict runs an optimizer step on the exchange it judged, moving the weights toward a rewarded reply and away from a punished one, by an amount set by the prediction error. The words in the trace also gain or lose value, and that value reweights the association plan on the next turn. The signal ends up in the numbers, not in a tally.

Inference

🧠 reasoning: on
GPU: checking…
📦 presets: on
presets are the two things this program writes for you: the canned social replies and the bootstrap corpus with the connections it grows. Off ignores both - nothing is deleted - so every sentence is built from the relations you trained and the documents you loaded, and connections only the bootstrap corpus supports stop being read. Replies always use basic conjunction logic now; no sentence shape is picked from a bank either way.

Training

training hyperparameters

How a reply is made

there is no prompt to train here. A reply is one formulation of the whole network: the reasoning ranks the words your turn reaches, the network predicts its own next token, and the two are averaged at the mix weight in the CHAT tab. Training moves the connections and the tensors, not a habit of picking answers by hand.

Agent file

    

      
      
.meso is the native format: it carries every tensor, the tokenizer, the full weight editor network (word rows + connections as numeric tensors), the corpus and the training state. Nothing is ever written as a .gguf - this model does not exist as one. An older .gguf can still be opened so a file you already have is never stranded, and .agent/.json load as before.

Export
the only format: every tensor plus the full weight editor network (word rows and their connections as numeric tensors) and, if you want, the corpus — in one file. opens a menu with size XS–XL and 8 real precision levels (Q4_0 … F32) measured on your actual weights.
.meso is the only format this model is written as — there is no container to pick. A .gguf can still be opened so an older file is never stranded, but nothing is ever written as one: the type is not this model's shape.

words live here as numeric rows and connections, not as vocabulary regions. training writes corpus correlation into these connections, COMMIT bakes them into the tok_emb weights, and SAVE .MESO stores the whole editor network with the model.

    

    
Reasoning mode

    

      
reasoning: off

      
      
      
      

        

        

      

      
—

      
necessary — the connections the network stands on: weight, how many training runs measured it, and whether it is the only route between its words.

      

      
proposed — pairs the same evidence connects but no connection exists for. ADD writes a real weight you can then train and edit.

      

      
redundant — weak and bypassed: another route already joins the pair.

      

      

      
—

      
the reasoning reads the weights only: it scores every connection by how strongly it is held, how many training runs measured it, whether it is the only route between its two words, and how many neighbours the pair already shares — then it proposes the links that the same evidence says are missing. nothing is invented and nothing is applied without you pressing ADD.
